q: How many customers should a founder close before hiring a salesperson?
a: There is no fixed number, but most B2B founders are ready somewhere between five and fifteen paying customers. What matters more than the count is whether those deals look alike: a similar buyer, a similar problem and a similar path to signature. If every deal was different, keep selling until a pattern appears.

q: Should my first sales hire be a VP of Sales?
a: Usually not. A VP of Sales needs a working sales motion and a team to lead. Your first hire should be an experienced individual seller who is comfortable building process as they go. Hire a sales leader once you have a few sellers hitting their numbers and need someone to scale what works.

q: How long should the transition from founder-led sales take?
a: Plan for about one quarter. Move through three stages: the new seller shadows your calls, then runs calls with you present, then owns deals and brings you in only for key moments. Move on from each stage when it is working, not on a fixed date.

q: Should founders stay involved in sales after hiring a sales team?
a: Yes, as an executive sponsor rather than the person running deals. Founders should meet senior buyers on large or strategic deals, lead or attend the weekly deal review, and make sure what sellers hear from customers reaches the product team.
